title: Canonical constant Tate structure and the rational purity Frobenius square
statement:
Let $k_0$ be a finite field, $k$ an algebraic closure, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ a prime and $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Use the rational common-stage bounded constructible coefficient categories and operations of [def-pur-conventions], and the Weil fixed-pair categories of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let $X_0$ be separated and of finite type over $k_0$, with structure morphism $a_0:X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ smooth of relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $a:X\to s$. Let $g_X,g_s$ be geometric Frobenius, $Q=Lg_X^*$, $P=Lg_s^*$, $F=Ra_!$, $G=Ra^!$, and $H(K)=La^*K(d)[2d]$. Let $\beta:PF\xrightarrow{\sim}FQ$ be canonical compact-support exchange and $e:QG\xrightarrow{\sim}GP$ its inverse's right adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Let $\gamma_K:H(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}G(K)$ be the canonical rational purity map of [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity]. Let $b_K:QH(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(PK)$ be pullback composition for $ag_X=g_sa$, followed by the canonical tensor, Tate-line and shift comparisons, using [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. Write $(\Lambda_s,\theta_0)$ and $(\Lambda_X,\theta_X)$ for the canonical constant pairs of [def-weil-constant-weil-structure], and write $\theta_{H,\mathrm{can}}$ for the structure on $\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ obtained by the canonical Tate twist and the pullback-shift comparison. Then the usual identification $La^*\Lambda_s\cong\Lambda_X$ carries the pullback of $\theta_0$ to $\theta_X$, and under its twisted and shifted identification $H(\Lambda_s)\cong\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ one has
$$\theta_{H,\mathrm{can}}=H(\theta_0)\circ b_{\Lambda_s},$$
$$G(\theta_0)\circ e_{\Lambda_s}\circ Q(\gamma_{\Lambda_s})=\gamma_{\Lambda_s}\circ\theta_{H,\mathrm{can}}.$$
These are identities in the common-stage category and use the rational Frobenius isomorphism, without requiring a Frobenius-stable integral lattice. The purity isomorphism here is exactly the inverse of the geometric dualizing identification of [cor-pur-adic-and-rational-smooth-dualizing-complexes].

proof.text: Auxiliary exchange construction: the two rationalExchange_endpoints equalities follow by explicitly unfolding the retained rational source/target definitions, then by the compact branch of modelRationalFunctor, the prescribed rationalLeft endpoints and geometric Frobenius pullback. Give rationalBeta and betaAtStage their explicit functor-object endpoint types and elaborate the five conjugation factors separately. Project the same coefficient system with explicit geometric instances. Before common-stage inclusion, transport the rational arrow along the definitional equality of the two inherited rational-stage category structures, proved by unfolding their definitions. This preserves the original conjugation factors and their normalization while limiting unfolding of constructed pullbacks and coefficient structures. For exceptionalMate_isIso, [lem-pod-semilinear-field-operation-lifts] supplies the source and target common-stage Frobenius equivalences. Apply [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences] to the inverse of the recorded beta and the prescribed exceptional adjunction twice. Its resulting morphism is definitionally exceptionalMate.

Identify each rationalBeta with RationalWeilPurity.betaComponent using the rational compactification-exchange normalization. The generic transport_hom_of_heq lemma cancels its two functor endpoint transports. At every finite stage this identifies betaAtStage with the already constructed CommonWeilPurity.beta component. Use that natural isomorphism as witness for beta_existsUnique. For uniqueness, every common-stage object is literally the inclusion of its own stage object; Iso.ext and NatTrans.ext reduce the claim to the two component normalization equations.

The normalized unit constructors are reexported unchanged from CommonConstantUnitFrobenius. Apply commonUnit_frobenius at pointMap to obtain the first identity; all geometric instances are inherited exactly as in Square.

Use the common-stage natural tensor comparison of derivedPullbackTensorIso. Its naturality at the normalized unit identification, followed by bifunctoriality of tensor and the first identity, proves that canonicalSourceTheta equals sourceSquare followed by H(theta₀). The fixed shifted Tate-line map is retained in both composites.

Use the common-stage clause of rational_weil_purity_naturality_mate. commonFrobeniusSquare_eq identifies its b component with sourceSquare, and beta_existsUnique plus component extensionality identifies the chosen beta with CommonWeilPurity.beta. The canonical purity maps are definitionally the same commonIso.

The two counit equations identify the purity Frobenius conjugate with mateEquiv of beta.inv by injectivity of the inverse adjunction hom-equivalence and Mathlib mateEquiv_counit. Purity naturality at theta₀ and cancellation of Q(gamma) with its inverse give Q(gamma) followed by e followed by G(theta₀) equals b followed by H(theta₀) followed by gamma. Substitute the second identity.
